subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add native token-mode Gateway principals for per-user session isolation, and if so should this issue own only user identity or also the scoped service-token primitive from the related issue?
rationale: The request changes public auth config, bearer matching, caller identity, scope semantics, session-key derivation, and audit/security boundaries, so implementation should wait for maintainer product and security direction.

options.title: Design unified Gateway principals
options.body: Keep this issue open as the user-principal track and coordinate it with scoped service tokens and chat author attribution before code lands.

options.title: Scope to session labels only
options.body: Limit this issue to per-token user labels and session derivation, leaving service-token scopes and dispatch lanes to the related scoped-token issue.

options.title: Route to external front layer
options.body: Treat Pinchy-style front-layer auth as the supported path and close core work unless a missing Gateway API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Design unified Gateway principals
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the user-principal track and coordinate it with scoped service tokens and chat author attribution before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The trusted-proxy work is the closest existing identity-bearing Gateway auth path and likely provides the best comparison point for this design choice.
